Clinical and Biochemical Information For each patient biochemical test for HDL, LDL, triglyceride concentration, total cholesterol, serum rheumatic factor, anti-CCP, CRP, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and urine creatinine must be available. In addition information regarding smoking habits and intake of over-the-counter drugs must be made available through a questionnaire. Age, duration of disease and gender must also be available. Flow cytometric Analyses Flow cytometric analyses of synovial fluid cells or cells from whole blood will be performed using the BD Biosciences FACSArray instrument, which measures emitted fluorescence light in four channels only, not five channels. This makes it necessary to aliquot cells and use fluorochrome conjugated antibodies in the way stated below. A labelling of the predominant cell types in synovial fluid, namely macrophage-like synoviocytes (type A synoviocytes) and fibroblast-like synoviocytes (type B synoviocytes) is added: FACS protocol 1. From each patient 2 x 3 FACS staining tubes (Axygen MCT-150-L-C) are set up (3 from SF and 3 from blood). 2. To 300 µl EDTA-anticoagulated whole blood are added 30 µl of a 100 µg/ml solution of human IgG (Sigma I-4506) in Staining Buffer (PBS pH 7.40 with 0.2% human serum albumin (Sigma A-1653) and 0.09% w/v sodium azide). Mixing, then standing at room temperature for 15 minutes.

Microscopic analyses Sections are evaluated by virtual microscopy using either a Hamamatsu NanoZoomer (Hamamatsu Denmark, Ballerup, Denmark), or a FV10i Laser scanning microscope (Olympus Denmark A/S; Ballerup, Denmark), and an Olympus BX51 reflected fluorescence system microscope equipped with selective AMCA, FITC and Texas-Red filters, and a DP70 digital camera (Olympus Denmark A/S; Ballerup, Denmark).

Flow cytometry analysis of RA synovial tissue cells Tissue RA synovial membranes will obtained from patients undergoing joint replacement surgery or synovectomy. Cell Preparation for flow cytometry from synovial tissue Single-cell suspensions of RA synovial tissue biopsies will be prepared by mechanical disruption followed by enzymatic digestion for 1-2 h using Liberase TL (Roche, Welwyn Garden City, UK) and DNAse (Sigma-Aldrich Ltd, Dorset, UK). After passing the cells through a nylon mesh to exclude debris, cells are washed and resuspended in RPMI-1640 medium (containing 10% (v/v) FBS) at a density of 1x106 cells/ml. For FACS analysis, dead cells are excluded with Live/Dead Fixable Aqua Dead Cell Stain (Life Technologies, Waltham, MA, USA). After gating on viable CD45+ cells within the monocytic gate, CD14 vs. CD15 staining was used to identify macrophages and infiltrating neutrophils. The following anti-human monoclonal antibodies from BD Biosciences (San Jose, CA, USA) will be used: CD14-APC (clone M5E2), CD15-PECy7 (clone HI98), CD45-
PerCP (clone TU116). Anti-human C5aR/CD88-PE (clone S5/1, Biolegend, London, UK) and mIgG2a-PE (clone MOPC-173, Biolegend, London, UK) will be used to assess C5aR expression. To block non-specific Fc receptor-mediated antibody binding, FcR Blocking reagent (Miltenyi Biotec, Lund, Sweden) is used prior to antibody staining. Stained cells are fixed in Fixation Buffer (BD Biosciences, San Jose, CA, USA). Samples will be acquired in a BD Fortessa flow cytometer (BD Biosciences, San Jose, CA, USA) and analyzed using FlowJo software (Tree Star, Ashland, OR, USA). Ethics Ethics Committee for London Riverside and for the Capital Region of Denmark and the Danish Data Protection Agency will be sought for permissions to carry out the study and handle the data. Statistics Student’s t-test will be used for group comparisons, Spearman’s Rank correlation test for correlations tests. To correct for multiple comparisons, Bonferoni correction will be applied. steps.title: Prepare and Fc-block Cells
steps.instruction: Prepare isolated synovial fluid (SF) cells and whole blood cells for staining by blocking Fc receptors.

substeps.instruction: Add 40 µl of a 100 µg/ml human IgG solution in Staining Buffer to 400 µl of isolated SF-cells (approximately 500,000 cells).
Mix and incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Aliquot Fc-blocked whole blood into three 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes (110 µl each).
Aliquot Fc-blocked SF cells into four 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tubes (90 µl each), leaving the remainder in a tube labeled 'Tube 8' for CD68 isotype staining.

steps.title: Stain Whole Blood Cells
steps.instruction: Apply fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies to the whole blood cell aliquots.

substeps.instruction: Tube 1 (Isotypes): Add 20 μl each of Isotype-PE (BioLegend 400114), Isotype-APC (BioLegend 400122), Isotype-PE-Cy7 (BioLegend 400126), and Isotype-APC-Cy7 (BioLegend 400128).
Tube 2 (Monocytes): Add 20 μl each of C5aR-PE (CD88) (BD 550494, Clone D53), CD16-APC-Cy7, CD11b-APC, and CD14-PE-Cy7.

Tube 3 (Neutrophils): Add 20 μl C5aR-PE (CD88) (BD 550494, Clone D53), 5 μl CD11b-APC-Cy7, 20 μl CD62L-PE-Cy7 (BioLegend 304822, Clone DREG-56), and 10 μl CD203c-APC (Miltenyi 130-092-344, Clone FR3-16A11, ms).

steps.title: Incubate and Wash Whole Blood Cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the stained whole blood cells and remove unbound antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Mix carefully and incubate for 40 minutes at 4ºC.
Wash cells twice with 1.0 ml Staining Buffer; mix carefully and centrifuge at RCF 300 x g for 8 minutes between washes, removing supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 200 ml BD FACS Lysing Solution (BD 349202), mix, and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Wash cells twice with 1.0 ml Staining Buffer; mix carefully and centrifuge at RCF 300 x g for 8 minutes between washes.
Resuspend cells in 150 μl Staining Buffer and transfer to a well in a round-bottom polypropylene microtiter plate (Nunc 267245).

steps.title: Stain Synovial Fluid Cells
steps.instruction: Apply fluorochrome-conjugated antibodies to the SF cell aliquots.

substeps.instruction: Tube 4 (Isotypes): Add 3 μl each of Isotype-PE (BioLegend 400114), Isotype-APC (BioLegend 400122), Isotype-PE-Cy7 (BioLegend 400126), and Isotype-APC-Cy7 (BioLegend 400128).
Tube 5 (Monocytes): Add 3 μl each of C5aR-PE (CD88) (BD 550494, Clone D53), CD16-APC-Cy7, CD11b-APC, and CD14-PE-Cy7.

Tube 6 (Neutrophils/Fibroblast-like synoviocytes): Add 3 μl C5aR-PE (CD88) (BD 550494, Clone D53), 1 μl CD11b-APC-Cy7, 3 μl CD62L-PE-Cy7 (BioLegend 304822, Clone DREG-56), and 3 μl CD90-APC (BD 559869, Clone SE).
Tube 7 (Macrophage-like synoviocytes): Add 3 μl C5aR-PE (CD88) (BD 550494, Clone D53). Note: Permeabilization for CD68 occurs after CD88 staining.
Tube 8 (Isotype control for macrophage-like synoviocytes): Add 10 μl anti- (BD kit 55607). Note: Permeabilization required.

steps.title: Permeabilize and Stain for CD68
steps.instruction: Permeabilize cells in Tubes 7 and 8 to allow intracellular staining of CD68.

substeps.instruction: Add 100 µl PBS with 1% formaldehyde to Tubes 7 and 8; incubate for 10 minutes at 4 ºC.
Add 600 µl Staining Buffer and 40 µl saponin solution (0.5% in PBS); incubate for 5 minutes at 4 ºC.
Centrifuge at RCF 300 x g for 8 minutes and remove supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 100 µl Staining Buffer.
Add 10 µl PE-anti-CD68 to Tube 7 and 10 µl PE-anti-IgG 2b (isotype control) to Tube 8.

steps.title: Incubate and Wash SF Cells
steps.instruction: Incubate and process the SF cell tubes for flow cytometry.

substeps.instruction: Vortex mix all tubes carefully and incubate for 40 minutes at 4ºC.
Wash cells twice with 1.0 ml Staining Buffer; mix carefully and centrifuge at RCF 300 x g for 8 minutes between washes, removing supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 200 ml BD FACS Lysing Solution (BD 349202), mix, and incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Wash cells twice with 1.0 ml Staining Buffer; mix carefully and centrifuge at RCF 300 x g for 8 minutes between washes.
Resuspend cells in 150 μl Staining Buffer and transfer to a well in a round-bottom polypropylene microtiter plate (Nunc 267245).

steps.title: Perform Flow Cytometry Analysis
steps.instruction: Calibrate the FACSArray flow cytometer and acquire sample data.

substeps.instruction: Check the FACSArray flow cytometer using SPHERO Rainbow Calibration Particles (8 Peaks) (BD 559123).
Set photomultiplier gains for FSC, SSC, Yellow, Red, Far Red, and NIR channels.
Perform spill-over compensation using BD Comp Beads (BD 51-90-9001291) and isotype control antibodies from Tube 1; save settings as a template.
Count samples from Tubes 1 to 8 with an injection volume of 100 µl at 2.0 µl per second.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue Sections
steps.instruction: Cut and store fixed paraffin embedded tissue sections.

substeps.instruction: Cut sections at a nominal thickness of 3 μm.
Mount on Superfrost®Plus microscope slides.
Store at -20°C until processing.

steps.title: Perform Immunohistochemical Staining
steps.instruction: Execute the immunostaining protocol for microscopy on tissue sections.

substeps.instruction: Deparaffinise sections in xylene and rehydrate through decreasing concentrations of alcohols.
Perform antigen retrieval in Tris-EGTA buffer (10mM; 0.5 mM), pH 9.0 in a microwave oven for 15 min.
Block endogenous peroxidase activity with 3% H2O2.
Block endogenous biotin by incubating with Avidin and Biotin blocking solutions for 10 min.
Block non-specific binding by incubating with TBS containing 3% skimmed milk, 7% donkey serum, 3% human serum, and 3.2 mg/ml Poly-L-Lysine (PLL) for 30 min.
Incubate primary antibodies (diluted in Tris buffer with 0.5% skimmed milk, 7% donkey, 3% human sera) overnight at 4°C.
Incubate secondary antibodies (same dilution) for 60 min at room temperature.
Perform first amplification: incubate with Vectastain ABC peroxidase kit (diluted in 0.1 M Tris-HCl buffer pH 7.5 with 0.5% Du Pont Blocking Reagent TNB) for 30 min.
Perform second amplification: incubate in biotinylated Tyramide for 6 min.
Perform final amplification: incubate with Vectastain ABC peroxidase kit (as previously described) for 30 min.
Develop chromogenic reaction with diaminobenzidin.
Counterstain nuclei with haematoxylin, rehydrate, clear in xylene, and mount with Eukitt.

steps.title: Perform Double-Immunofluorescence
steps.instruction: Execute double-immunofluorescence staining for C5aR and a second target.

substeps.instruction: Follow the immunohistochemical demonstration of C5aR as described above, but at the second amplification step, incubate with biotinylated Tyramide for 3 min.
Incubate with Vectastain ABC peroxidase kit (as previously described) for 30 min.
Perform final amplification by incubating with Alexa-594 conjugated Tyramide (diluted per manufacturer) for 6 min.
Perform second round of microwave oven treatment in Tris-EGTA buffer (10mM; 0.5 mM), pH 9.0 for 10 min.
Block endogenous peroxidase with 3% H2O2 and endogenous biotin with Avidin and Biotin blocking solutions for 10 min.
Block non-specific binding with TBS containing 3% skimmed milk, 7% donkey serum, and 3% human serum for 30 min.
Incubate second primary antibodies (diluted in Tris buffer with 0.5% skimmed milk, 7% donkey, 3% human sera) overnight at 4°C.
Incubate second secondary antibodies for 60 min at room temperature.
Perform final amplifications: incubate with Vectastain ABC peroxidase kit (as previously described) for 30 min, followed by incubation with Alexa-488 conjugated Tyramide.
Counterstain nuclei with Hoechst for 15 min and mount in fluorescence mounting media (Dako).
